title: LANs, WANs and Network Performance
intro: Catch up on the essential lesson knowledge with 15 auto-marked questions and a self-reviewed explanation.

questions.prompt: After one ascending bubble-sort pass on [5, 2, 4, 1], what is the list?

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the concepts, model and key definitions.

blocks.title: Computer networks
blocks.text: Two or more connected computers share data and resources, such as printers, files and an internet connection.

blocks.title: LAN compared with WAN
blocks.text: A LAN covers a small area such as a school. A WAN covers a larger area and may link multiple LANs.

blocks.title: Network performance
blocks.text: Bandwidth measures how much data can be transferred per second. Users share available capacity; wired and wireless media can have different limits.

blocks.title: Explain the effect
blocks.text: Do not claim all WANs are slower. Use the scenario to link bandwidth, demand or transmission media to the impact on performance.

blocks.title: Worked example · A trust links two schools in different towns. Explain why it needs a WAN and how busy connections may affect performance. [4 marks]
blocks.text: Schools in different towns cover a larger geographical area. A WAN links geographically distant networks [1] including the two school LANs [1]. Many simultaneous users share the available connection capacity [1], so file transfers may become slower [1]. Two WAN points and two linked performance points give four marking points.

items: Network — Two or more connected devices sharing resources.
LAN — Local Area Network; small geographical area.
WAN — Wide Area Network; larger geographical area.
Bandwidth — Data a connection can transfer per second.
Transmission media — Wires, optical fibre or wireless signals carrying data.
